boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten Hamilton spaces for studying, making, meeting, cultural programming, creative collaboration, and outdoor breaks, with access details from College sources.

cards.title: Settle into KJ Commons
cards.subtitle: An atrium for studying, meeting, and project work
cards.notes: Use the atrium for an informal study session, or move a group project into one of KJ’s purpose-built team rooms.
cards.short_summary: A light-filled academic commons with nearby rooms designed for collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton says the Kirner-Johnson Building has a comfortable atrium used by students, team rooms for group projects, and study spaces overlooking campus.
cards.access_notes: Team rooms and classrooms may be scheduled or occupied; use only spaces available for informal student use.

cards.title: Keep Working in Stryker
cards.subtitle: Burke Library’s named late-study room
cards.notes: Choose Stryker when your work runs beyond the main library schedule, and confirm current building-entry rules before arriving late.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated reading room configured for both extended study and flexible programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton’s account of Burke Library’s renovation identifies the Stryker All-Night Reading Room and its movable glass partition for programming use.
cards.source_title: Burke Library: A Space of Creation
cards.access_notes: The official source identifies it as the Stryker All-Night Reading Room; confirm current late-entry and academic-break access with Burke Library.

cards.title: Prototype Something in TECH Lab
cards.subtitle: Burke Library’s makerspace and production hub
cards.notes: Bring a project idea, consult a technologist or student tutor, and reserve production equipment or a booth when your work requires one.
cards.short_summary: A staffed creation space for digital media, VR/AR, 3D design, printing, and experimentation.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton describes TECH Lab as a hands-on workplace with VR/AR tools, 3D design and printing equipment, four production booths, tutors, and reservable resources.
cards.access_notes: Production booths, equipment, and some services require reservations or appointments; consult the TECH Lab page before visiting.

cards.title: Use Couper Between Sessions
cards.subtitle: A computer-equipped collaborative room in Burke Library
cards.notes: Check whether a workshop is scheduled; when the room is open, use its computers for research, media, or collaborative coursework.
cards.short_summary: A flexible teaching room that becomes a student computer workspace between scheduled events.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton says LITS classes and workshops occur in Couper Classroom and that its banks of computers are available for student use when events are not underway.
cards.source_title: Burke Library: A Space of Creation
cards.access_notes: Available for student use only when it is not hosting a class, workshop, training, or other scheduled event.

cards.title: Gather in Sadove’s Living Room
cards.subtitle: A reservable room inside the student center
cards.notes: Use the room for a student-group meeting or program, and submit a 25Live request when you need the space formally reserved.
cards.short_summary: A named student-center room intended for conversation, programming, meetings, and relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton lists the Sadove Living Room among the student-center spaces that may be reserved for programming or meetings.
cards.access_notes: Formal programs and meetings require a request through 25Live; student-organization requests receive priority.

cards.title: Meet on the Sun Porch
cards.subtitle: A smaller reservable space in Sadove Student Center
cards.notes: Pick the Sun Porch for a contained meeting or program, then reserve it through 25Live and plan around existing student-center bookings.
cards.short_summary: A distinct student-center setting that groups can schedule for campus activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton identifies the Sun Porch as one of the Sadove Student Center spaces available to reserve for programming or meeting use.
cards.access_notes: Programming and meeting use requires a 25Live reservation; availability depends on the student-center schedule.

cards.title: Build a Program in the Events Barn
cards.subtitle: A reservable venue in Beinecke Student Activities Village
cards.notes: Plan a student event here through 25Live, and bring complex setup needs to the Weekly Events Meeting before the program date.
cards.short_summary: A student-activities venue for organized programming, with advance scheduling and setup coordination.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton lists Fillius Events Barn as a reservable Beinecke Village programming room and states that alcohol is prohibited in the Events Barn.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through 25Live. Programs with substantial setup needs should be reviewed at the preceding Weekly Events Meeting.

cards.title: Connect at Days-Massolo
cards.subtitle: A campus center for cultural education and dialogue
cards.notes: Join a workshop, discussion, or identity-focused program; student groups can request DAYS 100 through 25Live for official events.
cards.short_summary: A home-like campus center supporting cultural learning, community programs, and peer dialogue.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton says students and faculty use the Days-Massolo Center for cultural education, workshops, panels, support groups, and official student-group events.
cards.source_title: Days-Massolo Multicultural Center - Workshops and Programs
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are Monday-Friday 8 a.m.-10 p.m. and Saturday-Sunday 10 a.m.-10 p.m.; event reservations use 25Live.

cards.title: Collaborate in Kennedy’s Common Space
cards.subtitle: An arts-building gathering area filled with natural light
cards.notes: Bring reading, sketches, or a small collaborative task and use the common furniture without entering specialized studios uninvited.
cards.short_summary: An open arts-center commons designed for studying, relaxing, gathering, and creative exchange.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton documents students studying, relaxing, congregating, and collaborating in the Kennedy Center’s first-floor common space.
cards.source_title: Kennedy Center for Theatre and the Studio Arts
cards.access_notes: Use the open common area; studios, shops, theatres, and production rooms may be restricted to classes or authorized users.

cards.title: Take a Reset in Root Glen
cards.subtitle: A wooded garden and ravine beside the campus core
cards.notes: Follow the established red-shale paths for a walk, sketching break, or quiet reset, and protect plantings by staying on the route.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus garden where a short walk can replace another indoor study break.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton describes Root Glen as a 7.5-acre wooded garden and ravine maintained for public enjoyment and educational use; its page also depicts a student sketching there.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions are seasonal; remain on established paths and follow posted campus or arboretum notices.
